text: This deposit can be used to defray the costs of removing abandoned bicycles of any operator that has gone bankrupt.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Lim Biow Chuan have also suggested requiring operators to provide bicycle parking spaces or docking stations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Operators have already helped to provide some of the yellow parking boxes at bus stops, and LTA will be able to impose requirements on them to do more under the licensing regime, if necessary.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Png Eng Huat suggested the implementation of docking stations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The experience of other countries is that docked systems tend to be unsustainable without private sponsorship or government subsidies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These tend to be more costly to set up, so, taxpayers or users would have to pay more for the use of the bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As Miss Cheng Li Hui, Mr Yee Chia Hsing and Mr Lim Biow Chuan have rightly pointed out, we should not just focus on the operators alone.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is also important to ensure that users act responsibly and considerately.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We feel that the most effective way of doing so is through the operators.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, LTA will require all licensed bicycle sharing operators to collectively ban users who repeatedly park the bicycles indiscriminately from using any bicycle sharing service for a period of time.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked about the effectiveness of geofencing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, geofencing will be done in addition to the other measures that I have outlined earlier.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Second, under the proposed licensing regime, LTA will require all licensed operators to complement global positioning system (GPS) geofencing with quick response (QR) code-enabled geofencing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And each designated parking area will have a unique QR code.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Chairman, to conclude, we have come far in making our transport system more inclusive and safer for all commuters.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also need the community’s support in instilling a culture of safety and civic-mindedness so that everyone can enjoy the benefits of active mobility.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Used safely and responsibly, bicycles and PMDs offer great convenience, promote a healthy lifestyle and is environmentally-friendly and will also help fulfil our vision of a car-lite society.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like what Er Dr Lee Bee Wah shared yesterday "make this a beautiful dream for all, not a nightmare." With our continued infrastructural enhancements, the use of technology and enhanced enforcement measures against reckless and irresponsible behaviour, I am confident that our future transport system, centred on public transport, will be safe and inclusive, leaving no one behind.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Mr Chairman, I have three clarifications for Second Minister Ng Chee Meng.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: So, I wonder whether we still need the taxi availability indicator since we have hit such a high level of satisfaction.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Second, the Minister mentioned that he will incorporate digital training into private hire car and taxi drivers' course curriculum.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: My concern is more with new entrants coming into this industry.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: If they were to be displaced later by AV, perhaps we should better advise them as to how to make a career choice when they come to thinking about driving as a vocational skill.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Third, I welcome the move to regulate Uber and Grab-type of third-party apps operator.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I was wondering whether LTA will adopt part of the tripartite workgroup's recommendation for self-employed persons, as announced by Minister Josephine Teo earlier this week concerning protection and coverage that we should be giving to self-employed persons, particularly when it comes to regulating these two operators.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for his questions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As I have said in this Chamber for the last two years, we are monitoring but are always open to a review.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The second question is basically on career counselling.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: That, I think, is not difficult to do.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We can easily put up a couple of preambles for the public coming in to apply for the licence.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: On the last part, we will study the proposal.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Mr Chairman, my questions are for the Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: First, regarding his answers to me in respect of my suggestion for the TSS, the arguments the Senior Minister of State has raised regarding my suggestion for non-crossing, he mentioned about vessel bunching and the suggested U-turn spot.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The suggestion I have is more akin to a safer flow, because vessels will be moving, imagine by analogy to land transport.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: What I am suggesting is something like imagine cars merging and going into a one-lane highway and entering an expressway, all in the same direction.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: But at this moment, the ships are coming out from the various anchorages and terminals, the eastern and western anchorages, the terminals at Tuas and Keppel, and they are crossing over.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, this is akin to something like on the road, they are coming across to an uncontrolled multi-junction where there is no traffic light, and we are relying on the rules of the road.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: And seafarers will know that rules of the road alone are not sufficient to prevent a collision.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State to reconsider this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I know that, ultimately, it is a cost-benefit analysis.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I know that time is important for our port, for PSA.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: But where I am coming from is a safety imperative.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: We cannot afford any accident, especially the kind of accident that will create oil pollution, for example, which will be a big disaster for Singapore and, hopefully, it will never happen.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I would also like to suggest regarding my AIS suggestion for Government-enabled vessels, perhaps this is a little bit awkward as a matter of diplomacy—

speaker: The Chairman
text: Can the Member keep it as a clarification, rather than a speech, please?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: —but I would really like the Government to consider raising a dialogue on this at the IMO-level.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: On the issue of enforcement between bikes and PMDs, I have said this in my cut, and I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State to consider a more consistent enforcement against bike offences.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: For example, I do not see there is any difference between a PMD travelling on the road, and a bike travelling against the direction of beating the red light.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I think that the enforcement measure should be equal.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, safety is paramount along the Straits of Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Currently, there are already existing safety measures put in place ‒ code of conduct for the vessels when they do the crossings.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But we will continue to monitor this very carefully, bearing in mind, like what Mr Dennis Tan has said, safety is paramount.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the turning on of the AIS for government as well as naval vessels, we are abiding by the IMO Convention, and I think this is widely accepted by many jurisdictions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the enforcement on bikes and PMDs, we take this very seriously.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I have explained in my last Parliamentary Sitting, there are measures put in place to step up enforcement action.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Chairman, on behalf of Bukit Panjang residents, I would like to thank the Minister for Transport for announcing the upgrading of Bukit Panjang LRT.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Just one clarification – will the upgrading work include building a noise barrier because some parts of the LRT are very close to the HDB flats?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In fact, this year's Budget is very close to the budget for MINDEF which, traditionally, has been the highest.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Some are medium-term and long-term projections ‒ I cannot remember ‒ but the huge increase, much of it is capital expenditure (capex).

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Unfortunately, the one-off can last several years, because the projects are so huge, especially T5.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It will really be our largest integrated project for the Government in the history of modern Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Likewise, my other MRT projects are also multi-year projects.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, it imposes a heavy responsibility on us to make sure that we spend every single dollar very carefully and, at the same time, be on a constant lookout for ways and means to save money.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For example, the Changi East Coast integrated depot that we highlighted a few days ago was one of those efforts.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Chairman, I have a question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Would the Senior Minister of State share why LTA is not in favour of reducing the number of signalised junctions with shared green time from 90%, in view of the fact that such junctions do present a safety concern for all road users, apart from the given answer of ensuring a smoother flow of traffic, which, for some urban junctions, it is never an issue?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As it is, like what the Member has mentioned, about 90% of signalised crossings in Singapore have shared green time.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Many of them already come with a set of standard safety features.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I have already explained in my reply this included integrated pedestrian countdown timers and the turning pockets for cars to stop and wait for the pedestrians to complete their crossing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, we also have added safety enhancements which include things like "Give Way to Pedestrian" signs at the junction, of which some may be static while some may be Light Emitting Diode (LED)-lighted to enhance their visibility.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have also implemented lighted road studs along the crossings, to also increase visibility for drivers and alert them to the possible presence of pedestrians.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I have also mentioned in my reply, there are special traffic light settings to allow the pedestrians to have a headstart in crossing the road, so that by the time the driver can make the turning, the position of the pedestrian will be more obvious to the driver.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We understand the concerns on the ground and we are doing what we can to ensure safety at signalised junctions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: That also includes public education on good road safety practices, as well as to remind drivers that it is their responsibility to look out for pedestrians.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The very enthusiastic, as always, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I have three clarifications for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: First, I am glad to hear that the Ministry is supporting the registration of e-scooters.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: My question is: will the registration be extended to other motorised PMDs?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: My second question is: in my speech, I asked about the on-road cycling lanes at Tanah Merah Coast Road.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: What is the result of the piloting, and will more such on-road cycling lanes be built?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Lastly, among the infrastructure improvements for the safety of cyclists and pedestrians, I would like to ask for a safer cross-junction between cycling lane and the pedestrian crossing, as what I have suggested in my speech, the one that I have seen in Copenhagen.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And if the Senior Minister of State needs a place to pilot, I will offer him the one at Naval Base Primary School main gate.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is based on the recommendation of the Active Mobility Advisory Panel.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They have also studied the possibility of registering other PMDs, especially those that are motorised.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But we are taking a risk-based approach because we feel that the speed that can be generated by the e-scooter is actually much faster than the other smaller-scale PMDs like unicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are not saying we will never implement registration for them, but at this moment, we accept the recommendation of the Advisory Panel to start registering e-scooters first.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But we also do understand that because of the limitations of the size of many roads in Singapore, it is very difficult to implement this islandwide.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: You may have certain roads that are wide enough for such a cycling lane, but it may come to a point where certain roads become narrow and not implementable.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On the Member's third point on infrastructure developments, yes, we are looking at how to improve the infrastructure to make active mobility more conducive.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the Member's particular suggestion about certain crossing zones, drawing from her example of some concerns outside the school, I think we do have pedestrian-priority zones that can be implemented at areas that the Member has mentioned.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Meaning to say that, if you do designate this particular area as a pedestrian-priority zone, then cyclists will have to give way to pedestrians or to slow down whenever cyclists approach such a junction.

text: Transporting the expertise over to land transport should not be too difficult.

text: They, in fact, used the exhibition to demonstrate to some of us how it could be done.
